results.title: DGX Spark partner FAQ: 70% share, payouts, tax | GPUwerk
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
By Samuel Seidel · Published October 3, 2026 · Updated October 21, 2026

Quick answers for owners listing a Spark on GPUwerk Platform: you keep 70% of every rented hour, get paid monthly in euros, in CZK, or through Wise, and can unlist any time. Each answer summarises the partner agreement and the console's rules; the agreement you accept with your application is the binding text.

What is GPUwerk Platform?

GPUwerk's programme for DGX Spark owners: your Spark stays at your premises, runs GPUwerk's locked system, and GPUwerk rents its hours to its customers as a separate Partner product. You receive 70% of what renters are charged for your machine, $0.55 for each hour at the $0.79 Partner Spark price. You manage it under Hosting at console.gpuwerk.com, with the same account you would rent with.

...

Can GPUwerk change the terms?

Yes, with at least 15 days' notice (clause 11 of the partner agreement). You can accept the new version or unlist your Spark before it takes effect.

results.title: Enverge alternative: GPUwerk vs Enverge for DGX Spark rental
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
By Samuel Seidel · Published October 11, 2026 · 7 min read

Enverge and GPUwerk both rent a dedicated NVIDIA DGX Spark by the minute. Since Enverge raised its rate, GPUwerk is cheaper per running hour ($0.79 against $0.85). Enverge lists 4 TB of storage against 1 TB, and has a four-node tier. GPUwerk is in the Czech Republic under an EU operator with a published GDPR Article 28 DPA, and a stopped GPUwerk instance keeps its workspace at 75% of the rate, where Enverge bills until you delete the instance and its data. I run GPUwerk, so read this with that in mind. Every Enverge figure below comes from Enverge's own pages, checked on 9 November 2026 and linked at the end.

...

| | GPUwerk | Enverge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One Spark, running | $0.79/hour on demand. (advantage) | $0.85/hour on demand. The Spark page marks founder support "during beta". |
| Clusters | Two nodes at $1.79/hour (256 GB across two nodes, not one memory pool). No four-node option. | Two nodes at $1.90/hour, four nodes at $4.50/hour. Enverge's docs also say the 256 GB is two 128 GB pools, not one address space. |
| Billing | Per minute from prepaid credit. Account plus a $20 minimum top-up. | Metered in minutes from create to delete, "rounded up per billing bucket", invoiced daily to a card on file. |
| Pausing | Stop keeps the machine and the workspace at 75% of the rate ($0.59/hour). Terminate ends billing and deletes the workspace. (advantage) | "Stopping does not pause billing." Charges end only when you delete the instance, and deleting destroys its data. |
| Storage | 1 TB NVMe. GPUwerk keeps no copy of the workspace, so backups are yours. | 4 TB NVMe, listed as "Ephemeral or Persistent" on the Spark page. The terms say storage is ephemeral, with no backups or snapshots. (advantage) |
| Fixed-term booking | Monthly reservations from 1 to 24 months, up to 35% off. A 12-month term is $432.53 a month. | Reservations of 1 to 5 consecutive days at a flat $16.80 a day, paid up front. Nothing longer. |
| When nothing is free | The console shows live availability, and you can join a waitlist. | A free first-in, first-out queue. The docs say a wait "can run from hours to days" under heavy demand. |
| Inside the instance | Root in your own container on a dedicated Spark. On many Sparks it runs systemd and its own Docker daemon (docker run --gpus all works); others run a plain container without Docker, and you can't choose which. Browser terminal or SSH with your own key. | A container sandbox on dedicated, single-tenant hardware. Docker is preinstalled inside it and can reach the GPU with the NVIDIA runtime. SSH through Enverge's relay. |
| Where the machine is | Czech Republic (EU-Central) on GPUwerk's own tiers. The Partner tier runs at an independent partner's premises, in an EU or EEA country unless you choose a location outside it. You may use any data on it. (advantage) | The homepage names three fleet regions: us-west-1 (US), br-east-1 (Brazil) and eu-south-1 (Greece). No page I read says which region the Sparks are in. Customer traffic goes through a relay in Amsterdam. |
| Contract and data protection | PRINT IT! SE, Prague. A published GDPR Article 28 DPA. (advantage) | Enverge Corp, Delaware, under Delaware law. The terms list GDPR rights you can exercise by email. They do not mention a data processing agreement. |
| SLA | None published. | None. The terms say there is no SLA or uptime guarantee. |
| Other hardware | RTX 5090 (32 GB) at $0.89/hour; single GPUs from the L4 to the B300 at $0.49 to $6.49/hour, and whole 8-GPU servers from $21.52/hour. See the GPU catalog. | RTX Pro 6000 at $1.95/hour and Mac Studio M5 Ultra at $2.50; H100 at $4, H200 at $5.50 and B300 at $9.50 on request. |

Checked 2026-11-09. Highlighted cells mark the stronger option for that row. Enverge sources are listed at the end of this page. GPUwerk figures come from GPUwerk's published pricing, the tenant environment page and the DPA.

...

On running time alone GPUwerk is now cheaper. The $0.06 an hour is $2.40 over a 40-hour week of use ($31.60 at GPUwerk, $34.00 at Enverge) and $9.60 over 160 hours ($126.40 against $136.00). Over a full month of 730 hours, Enverge's homepage puts a Spark at about $621, against $576.70 at GPUwerk's on-demand rate, and a 12-month GPUwerk term is $432.53 a month.

...

- Enverge: stopping does not pause billing, so the instance runs on at $0.85 for all 24 hours, which is $20.40.

...

Not on demand any more. Enverge raised its rate to $0.85 an hour for one Spark, against GPUwerk's $0.79, and $1.90 for two nodes against $1.79, checked on 9 November 2026. Enverge also keeps billing a stopped instance at the full rate until you delete it, while GPUwerk bills a stopped instance at 75% and keeps the workspace. The exception is Enverge's one-day reservation: $16.80 for 24 hours is less than a full day on either on-demand rate.

results.title: Primcast vs GPUwerk Platform: rent out a DGX Spark for $0.55 per rented hour
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
By Samuel Seidel · Published October 18, 2026 · Updated 21 October 2026 · 4 min read

On Primcast you pick a rent, keep running your own install, and renters reach the internet from your IP address. GPUwerk Platform is built for the GB10 and does the work for you: a fixed 70% of every rented hour, $0.55 at the $0.79 Partner Spark price, paid monthly in EUR, in CZK, or through Wise. Renters stay isolated from your network, their traffic leaves through GPUwerk, and you can use your Spark free whenever it is idle.

...

| | GPUwerk Platform | Primcast |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who sets the price | GPUwerk: renters pay $0.79 an hour for a Partner Spark, the same for every owner. Nothing for you to price. | You set a monthly rent, and optionally hourly, daily and weekly ones. Primcast sets the separate price the renter pays. |
| Fee or deduction | You get 70% of what renters are charged: $0.55 per rented hour at $0.79. | Primcast says it deducts nothing from the rent you set. Its terms put your own bank's fees and the payment provider's conversion charge on you. |
| What an hour pays | 70% of every charged hour, including stopped time a renter keeps reserved. | Your monthly rent divided by 720 for each hour rented and online. Offline time during a rental earns nothing and may be refunded to the renter. |
| Payout cadence | Monthly, within 30 days of month end, from a self-billing statement. | Monthly, within the first ten days of the following month, no minimum. |
| Payout method | EUR by SEPA, CZK to a Czech bank, or Wise to almost every country, to an account in your name. | Bank transfer through Primcast's payment partner, in your account's currency. The bank must be in a country that partner can pay out to. |
| Location | Owners in any country not under EU sanctions can join. Any-location bookings stay in the EEA; a Spark outside the EEA is rented by renters who choose its country. | No country list. Home and office lines are normal listings. Renters can filter for machines in the EU, EEA and adequacy countries. |
| Network and CGNAT | Outbound WireGuard over UDP; no port forwarding or public IP. At least 300 Mbit/s down, 100 Mbit/s up, outbound HTTPS and UDP. | One outbound SSH connection to a relay on TCP 2222. No public IP needed, CGNAT works, no minimum upload speed; measured speeds appear on the listing. |
| Whose IP renters use | GPUwerk's. Renter traffic exits from GPUwerk's address, and burn-in checks that a renter container cannot reach your router. | Your own public IP. Primcast's terms say it does not filter that traffic and that third parties may attribute a renter's activity to your address. |
| GB10 machines that qualify | Any 128 GB NVIDIA GB10 machine you own outright. All eight GB10 models confirmed working on 19 October 2026. | Names the NVIDIA DGX Spark (Founders Edition included), ASUS Ascent GX10 and ZGX nano, and its marketplace page describes setup for "a DGX Spark or other GB10 machine". |
| Your OS | GPUwerk's locked system, installed from a USB stick, which erases the machine. GPUwerk handles firmware and OS updates. | Kept. Your DGX OS, driver, CUDA and container runtime stay; the agent adds podman and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. You keep root. |
| Rental terms | Renters pay per use at $0.79 an hour. Unlist any time, no notice, no minimum period. | Monthly rent, plus hourly, daily or weekly if you offer them. You can reprice, pause or remove a machine when it is not rented; a running rental keeps the price it was ordered at. Removing the agent mid-rental ends it and counts as unavailability. |
| Verification | TPM attestation, at least 1 hour of burn-in with one restart, then a GPUwerk review. | Identity verification through payout setup. Checks on GPU identity, memory, thermals, load stability, storage throughput and network path; unlimited retries. |
| Using it yourself | "Use my Spark" is free whenever it is idle, in an isolated instance. | You choose the availability you sell and pause the listing to take the machine back. The DGX Spark desktop stays usable until someone rents it.

results.title: DGX Spark vs RTX PRO 6000: 128 GB, 273 GB/s vs 96 GB, 1.8 TB/s
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
The RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell has 1,792 GB/s of memory bandwidth against the Spark's 273 GB/s, about 6.6 times more, so it decodes several times faster on any model that fits in its 96 GB. The Spark holds 32 GB more (128 GB against 96 GB), is a whole computer rather than a card, and rents by the minute for $0.79 an hour. I run GPUwerk, which rents DGX Sparks and does not rent a PRO 6000, so weigh everything below with that in mind.

...

| --- | --- | --- |
| Memory | 128 GB LPDDR5x, unified (advantage) | 96 GB GDDR7 ECC |
| Memory bandwidth | 273 GB/s | 1,792 GB/s (about 6.6 times) (advantage) |

...

| Decode ceiling, 70B model at 4-bit (37 GB) | About 7.4 tok/s; GPUwerk-measured 6.0 tok/s (Llama 3.3 70B AWQ) | About 48 tok/s.

...

| Fits gpt-oss-120b at MXFP4 | Yes | Yes |

...

| Rent options | GPUwerk, $0.79/h, per minute |

...

GPUwerk rents a dedicated Spark at $0.79 an hour, billed per minute from prepaid credit. An hour of your own prompts on a Spark tells you whether a model's quality is enough, and whether 6 tok/s or 60 tok/s is tolerable for your use. A first top-up of $20 or more gets $10 extra credit.

results.title: Vast.ai vs GPUwerk Platform: host a DGX Spark for $0.55 per rented hour
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
By Samuel Seidel · Published October 11, 2026 · Updated October 21, 2026 · 4 min read

Vast.ai is a marketplace for every kind of GPU. GPUwerk Platform is built for one machine: the GB10 in your DGX Spark. You keep a fixed 70% of every rented hour, $0.55 at the $0.79 Partner Spark price, paid monthly in EUR, in CZK, or through Wise. There is no price to manage, no Ubuntu to maintain and no router port to open, and the Spark stays yours to use whenever it is idle.

...

| | GPUwerk Platform | Vast.ai host |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who sets the price | GPUwerk: $0.79 an hour for a Partner Spark, the same for every owner. Nothing for you to price. | The host sets the price per listing. |
| Platform share | 70% of what renters are charged: $0.55 per rented hour at $0.79. | Not stated. Vast.ai replaced its hosting fee with an internal surcharge in June 2024 and says the prices hosts set are the prices they earn. |
| Payout method | From a self-billing statement: EUR by SEPA, CZK to a Czech bank, or Wise to almost every country, to a verified account in your name. | Wise, PayPal or Stripe. |
| Payout frequency | Monthly, within 30 days of month end. | Weekly invoices on Fridays. First payout can take up to two weeks. |
| OS and drivers | None to administer. GPUwerk's install from a USB stick erases the machine and puts on a locked system; GPUwerk handles firmware and OS updates. | You install Ubuntu and the NVIDIA drivers, then the Vast hosting software, and keep them working. |
| Ports and network | No port forwarding: an outbound-only WireGuard tunnel. At least 300 Mbit/s down, 100 Mbit/s up, outbound HTTPS and UDP. | You open the network ports on your router. |
| Home-network isolation | Renters run in containers on a separate network, the Spark's firewall drops devices on your LAN, and renter traffic exits from GPUwerk's address. Burn-in tests the isolation. | Verified Hosts run workloads in Docker containers. Vast.ai's host pages give no guidance on keeping the rest of your LAN away from the machine. |
| Verification | TPM attestation, at least 1 hour of burn-in with one restart, then a GPUwerk review. | Fully automated, on reliability (sustained uptime of 99.99% or more), configuration, DLPerf score, and supply and demand. Datacenter GPUs such as H100 and B200 are named as the priority; a GB10 is not on that list. |
| Leaving or unlisting | Any time, no notice, no minimum period. | Unlisting stops new rentals, but running contracts continue to the rental end date you set in your offer, and you must keep the machine online until the latest one. |
| Using the machine yourself | "Use my Spark" is free whenever it is idle, in an isolated instance. | You keep your Ubuntu install and your login. During a rental the hardware cannot be used for any other purpose, and Vast.ai asks hosts to run their own jobs only through its Jobs tab or `create job` command. |
| Support during setup | GPUwerk support helps during the install and reviews the machine after burn-in. All eight GB10 models confirmed working on 19 October 2026. | None for setup. Vast.ai says it does not offer support for getting your machine working; hosts help each other on Discord. |

results.title: Make money with your DGX Spark: $0.55 an hour, paid monthly
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
By Samuel Seidel · Published October 3, 2026 · Updated October 28, 2026

Your DGX Spark can earn while you are not using it. List it on GPUwerk Platform and you keep 70% of every hour a renter pays for: $0.55 an hour at the $0.79 Partner Spark price, paid monthly in euros. No shipping, no minimum listing period, and the Spark stays yours to use whenever it is idle. Earnings depend on renter demand and are not guaranteed.

...

$0.55 for every hour a renter is charged at the full rate, which is 70% of $0.79. That is $13.27 a day if your Spark is rented around the clock. When a renter keeps a stopped instance reserved, they pay 75% of the rate and you still earn about $0.41 an hour.

...

A Spark rented every hour earns $4,844.28 a year. That pays back a Founders Edition bought at $4,699 (the US list price from February 2026) in about a year and one at $6,950 (since 2 October 2026) in about 17 months, before running costs. Prices and dates are on the DGX Spark price page.

...

When and how am I paid?

Monthly, on a self-billing statement converted to euros at the ECB rate for the month's last day. We pay within 30 days of month end by SEPA in EUR, in CZK to a Czech bank, or through Wise to almost every country; amounts under €20 roll over.

results.title: ASUS Ascent GX10 vs DGX Spark: same GB10, what differs
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
The ASUS Ascent GX10 and NVIDIA's DGX Spark Founders Edition use the same GB10 chip with 128 GB of LPDDR5x at 273 GB/s, so the memory-bandwidth ceiling on model speed is the same; GPUwerk has not benchmarked a GX10. Warranty does not separate them either: both vendors state one year on their own pages. What is left is price for the storage tier you need, availability and firmware cadence, and neither NVIDIA's product page nor ASUS's product or US eShop page showed a price when I checked on 11 October 2026.

...

| | NVIDIA DGX Spark Founders Edition | ASUS Ascent GX10 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chip | NVIDIA GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip | Same GB10 chip |
| Memory | 128 GB LPDDR5x. NVIDIA's page lists a 64 GB GB10 configuration as coming soon, sold only through OEM partners | 128 GB LPDDR5x. The Register (2 October 2026) names ASUS among the partners for a $4,999 64 GB version; ASUS's pages list only 128 GB |
| Bandwidth | 273 GB/s (NVIDIA) | 273 GB/s (same chip, inferred) |
| Storage options | Up to 4 TB NVMe, self-encrypting (NVIDIA) | 1 TB PCIe 4.0 M.2 base, up to 4 TB (ASUS specs); ASUS's FAQ names 1 TB and 4 TB SKUs and also mentions 2 TB |
| US price | Reported $6,950 for 128 GB on 2 October 2026 (The Register). NVIDIA's product page showed no price. A forum user wrote on 2 September 2026 that NVIDIA's store still sold it at $4,699 | No price on ASUS's product page or US eShop page on 11 October 2026. A forum user reported ASUS eShop prices of $6,000, $7,000 and $8,000 for 1, 2 and 4 TB on 2 September 2026 (user post, unconfirmed) |
| EU price | Not verified | Not verified. On 2 September 2026 one forum user wrote of buying two 1 TB units from a German retailer for EUR 3,680 excluding VAT the month before, without saying whether that was per unit; another gave about $5,500 as the cheapest 1 TB retail price he found in Europe (user posts) |
| Warranty | 1 year from purchase for a new unit (NVIDIA) | 1-year limited hardware warranty (ASUS). The ASUS US eShop states all sales are final, with returns only for defective units under warranty |
| Size and weight | 150 x 150 x 50.5 mm, 1.2 kg (NVIDIA) | 150 x 150 x 51 mm, 1.48 kg (ASUS specs) |
| Firmware source | NVIDIA DGX OS releases; the newest listed is July 2026, and the current software table shows DGX OS 7.5.0 (release notes) | ASUS support site package and ISO; the update FAQ was last updated 25 March 2026 and cites DGX OS 7.2.3 |
| Idle power after updates | NVIDIA's January 2026 release added ConnectX-7 hot-plug, saving up to 18 W when the adapter is unused (release notes) | A forum post dated 26 February 2026 said an ASUS fix was still pre-release (thread). I found no later ASUS statement |
| Available from | NVIDIA Marketplace, Amazon, Micro Center and PNY (NVIDIA); GPUwerk lists it without a price (ask for a price) | ASUS and retailers; GPUwerk lists it without a price (ask for a price) |
| GPUwerk Platform support | Qualifies; firmware keys published on the requirements page | Qualifies; firmware keys published, TPM ships turned off |

...

The forum thread mixes dates, regions and currencies, and its numbers disagree: one user wrote that a GX10 had been under $4,000 on Amazon and was now $6,700, and the Swiss and German posts do not line up with the US ones. The Founders Edition moved the same way: a forum user put it at $4,699 in NVIDIA's store on 2 September 2026, and The Register reported $6,950 a month later, blaming memory prices. Older articles therefore quote prices that no longer apply. For the 128 GB machine, the useful comparison is the same storage tier from each seller on the day you order, including shipping and VAT.

results.title: GB10 machines compared: DGX Spark, ASUS GX10, Dell, HP, Lenovo
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
By Samuel Seidel · Published October 11, 2026 · Updated October 19, 2026

NVIDIA, ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, MSI, Gigabyte and Acer all sell machines built on the same NVIDIA GB10 Superchip with 128 GB of LPDDR5x at 273 GB/s, so the choice comes down to storage, price, warranty, chassis, firmware and whether you can get one. On 11 October 2026 I could verify a dated European price for exactly one of the eight (the Lenovo ThinkStation PGX, EUR 4,579 excluding VAT at Bechtle Belgium), so apart from a reported US price for NVIDIA's own machine, every price cell below says "check vendor" instead of repeating a figure that may predate NVIDIA's 2 October price move. I run GPUwerk, which rents and sells GB10 machines, so read this as written by an interested party.

On 2 October 2026 The Register reported that the 128 GB DGX Spark had moved to $6,950, and that a 64 GB version will be sold only through Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI at around $4,999 (The Register, read 2026-10-11). NVIDIA's DGX Spark page lists the 64 GB configuration as exclusive to OEM partners and shows no price (read 2026-10-11). Everything on this page is the 128 GB machine unless it says otherwise. I did not find a ship date for the 64 GB version, so I give none.
